title: The 1983 Aviation Paper Every AI User Needs to Read
alt_title_1: Lisanne Bainbridge's Ironies of Automation Explained for AI
alt_title_2: How Over-Relying on AI Dulls the Judgment You Need Most
description_hook: In 1983, engineering psychologist Lisanne Bainbridge published 'Ironies of Automation' in Automatica, showing why automating routine work erodes human readiness for high-stakes emergencies. Here is how to stay sharp in the AI era.

scenes.headline: A 1983 Cockpit Warning Built for the AI Era
scenes.stat_label: HOW AUTOPILOT QUIETLY ERODES EXPERT SKILL
bullets: Written 40 years before modern large language models
Pinpointed why smart operators miss critical system errors
scenes.narration: Nearly forty years before modern chatbots arrived, a five-page aviation and control-room paper predicted the exact cognitive trap threatening today's AI users.

scenes.headline: Lisanne Bainbridge's Ironies of Automation
scenes.stat_label: EASY TASKS AUTOMATED • HARD FAILURES LEFT TO YOU
bullets: Machines absorb the easy 95% that kept human instincts sharp
Rusty humans are then expected to rescue rare 5% crises
scenes.narration: In 1983, psychologist Lisanne Bainbridge published Ironies of Automation in the journal Automatica. When machines take over ninety-five percent of routine work, human skill rusts right before the hardest five-percent emergency.
scenes.source: Lisanne Bainbridge, Automatica, Vol. 19, No. 6, pp. 775-779 (1983)

scenes.headline: From Sharp Architect to Passive Rubber-Stamper
scenes.left_body: Prompts from blank page -> accepts fluent errors unchallenged
scenes.right_body: Sketches thesis solo first -> uses AI to test & accelerate
scenes.narration: Outsourcing every first draft, calculation, and diagnosis turns sharp professionals into passive rubber-stampers who can no longer spot a confident AI error.

scenes.headline: Log 10 Manual Minutes Before Every Prompt
scenes.stat_label: SOLO SKELETON + AI LEVERAGE = SHARP OUTPUT
scenes.stat_subtext: 10m manual outline first -> preserves intuition & catches flaws
scenes.narration: Fly manually first: spend ten quiet minutes sketching your own logic, numbers, or structure before asking AI to challenge or accelerate your draft.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin protocol based on Bainbridge (1983) & Lee et al., CHI (2025)

scenes.headline: Automate Drudgery, Never Your Core Judgment
scenes.stat_label: KEEP YOUR MANUAL FLIGHT HOURS ALIVE
bullets: Offload formatting, boilerplate, and tedious data cleanup
Keep problem framing and verification strictly in your hands
scenes.narration: Automate repetitive execution drudgery, never the raw cognitive reps that keep your domain judgment sharp when automated systems fail.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
